tasks.title: Bacterial culture — period growth
tasks.context: A culture starts at $N_0=500$ and multiplies by $3$ every $4$ hours: $N(t)=500(3)^{t/4}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=12$ the culture exceeds $40000$ individuals.
The continuous force $k=\ln(3)/4$ reproduces $N(t)$ for all $t$.
The elapsed time $t=12$ covers strictly more than three full growth periods of length $4$.
The culture doubles in every single growth period of length $4$.
The culture reaches $40000$ individuals at some time strictly before $t=12$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$N(12)=500\cdot(3)^{3}=13500$$

$$13500 \le 40000.$$

So the statement is False.

**B.** → True

Rewrite the period model as an exponential:

$$(3)^{t/4}=e^{(t/4)\ln(3)}=e^{kt}$$

with $k=\ln(3)/4\approx0.274653$. Thus the continuous force reproduces $N(t)$ identically.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$\frac{t}{\text{period}}=\frac{12}{4}=3$$

$$3 \le 3.$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

Each period multiplies by $3$, not necessarily by $2$. Doubling every period would require factor $2$. Here the factor is $3$, so the claim fails.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Solve $N(t)=40000$:

$$t=\frac{\ln(40000/500)}{k}\approx15.9548$$

$$15.9548 \ge 12.$$

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: $N(t)=500\cdot(3)^{t/4}$. Equivalent continuous force $k=\ln(3)/4\approx0.274653$. At $t=12$, after $3$ growth periods, $N\approx13500$. Time to reach $40000$ is $t=\ln(40000/500)/k\approx15.9548$.

tasks.title: Competing continuous and discrete forecasts
tasks.context: Two forecasts start at $200$: continuous $f(t)=200\,e^{0.02t}$ and discrete $g(t)=200\,(1.025)^{t}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=15$ the continuous model exceeds the discrete base-$1.025$ model.
The continuous force $0.02$ exceeds $\ln(1.025)$.
At $t=15$ the two models differ by less than $5\%$ relative to the larger value.
The continuous model doubles strictly sooner than the discrete model.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Read the two terminal levels from the overview (or the figure).

$$f(15)\approx269.9718$$

$$g(15)\approx289.6596$$

$$269.9718 \le 289.6596.$$

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Compute the discrete force and compare with $k$.

$$\ln(1.025)\approx0.024693$$

$$0.02 \le 0.024693.$$

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Relative gap against the larger level:

$$\frac{|f-g|}{\max(f,g)}\approx0.067969$$

$$0.067969 \ge 0.05.$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

$$t_{\mathrm{cont}}=\frac{\ln 2}{0.02}\approx34.6574$$

$$t_{\mathrm{disc}}=\frac{\ln 2}{\ln(1.025)}\approx28.071$$

$$34.6574 \ge 28.071.$$

So the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Algebraically,

$$\ln\frac{Pe^{kt}}{P a^{t}}=(k-\ln a)t$$

$$=(0.02-0.024693)\cdot15\approx-0.070389.$$

Direct evaluation of $\ln(f/g)$ recovers the same number, so the identity holds.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:
Continuous forecast $f(t)=200e^{0.02t}$ versus discrete $g(t)=200(1.025)^{t}$. At $t=15$:

$$f(15)\approx269.9718,\quad g(15)\approx289.6596.$$

Equivalent discrete force $\ln(1.025)\approx0.024693$. Doubling times $34.6574$ (continuous) and $28.071$ (discrete).

tasks.title: Onyx — continuous force versus discrete 1.6%
tasks.context: A demographer models the population of Onyx by $f(t)=10\,e^{0.016t}$, where $t$ is years after a census and $f(t)$ is measured in millions of residents. A rival analyst proposes replacing the continuous path by annual compounding at nominal rate $1.6\%$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=24$, the continuous model exceeds $16$ million.
Replacing $e^{0.016t}$ by $(1+0.016)^{t}$ leaves the path unchanged for every $t$.
Over a single year the continuous model multiplies the population by a factor strictly larger than $1+0.016$.
The continuous doubling time is strictly less than $40$ years.
At $t=24$, the discrete path $g(t)=10(1+0.016)^{t}$ lies strictly below the continuous path.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Substitute the recovered force into the continuous level formula.

$$f(24)=10\,e^{0.016\cdot24}$$

$$=10\,e^{0.384}$$

$$\approx14.6815$$

Compare with the claim.

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Two closed forms agree for all $t$ only when their one-year multipliers match.

$$1+0.016=1.016$$

$$e^{0.016}\approx1.016129$$

Since $1.016\neq e^{0.016}$, the discrete replacement $(1+0.016)^{t}$ is not identical to $e^{0.016t}$. At the concrete horizon $t=24$ the values already differ (14.6369 versus 14.6815).

So the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Under continuous force $k$, the exact one-year multiplier is $e^{k}$, not $1+k$.

$$e^{0.016}-1\approx0.016129$$

$$1+0.016=1.016$$

For $k>0$ the inequality $e^{k}>1+k$ holds, so the continuous year-over-year growth factor exceeds $1+0.016$.

$$1.016129 > 1.016.$$

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Doubling means $f(t)=2f(0)$, which forces $e^{kt}=2$.

$$t=\frac{\ln 2}{0.016}$$

$$t\approx43.3217$$

Compare with $40$:

$$43.3217 \ge 40.$$

So the statement is False.

**E.** → True

From the overview, we have $f(24)\approx14.6815$ and $g(24)\approx14.6369$. Compare those two levels directly:

$$g(24)=10(1+0.016)^{24}\approx14.6369$$

$$f(24)\approx14.6815$$

$$14.6369 < 14.6815.$$

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:
The overview recovers the continuous census model

$$f(t)=10\,e^{0.016t}$$

for Onyx, with $f$ in millions of residents. The continuous annual force is $k=0.016$. At $t=24$,

$$f(24)=10\,e^{0.016\cdot24}\approx14.6815$$

The naive discrete rival $g(t)=10(1+0.016)^{t}$ gives $g(24)\approx14.6369$. One-year continuous growth is $e^{k}-1\approx0.016129$, not the force $k$ itself. Doubling solves $e^{kt}=2$, so $t=\ln 2/k\approx43.3217$.

tasks.title: Newton cooling — ambient trap
tasks.context: A cup cools under Newton's law $T(t)=T_a+(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}$ with $T_0=75$, ambient $T_a=15$, and $k=0.051$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=37$ the temperature is not strictly below $30$.
At $t=37$ the temperature remains not strictly above ambient $T_a=15$.
As $t\to\infty$ the model temperature approaches the initial temperature $T_0$.
The temperature reaches $30$ at some time strictly before $t=37$.
The deviation from ambient at $t=37$ equals $(T_0-T_a)e^{-0.051\cdot37}$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Substitute into Newton's law.

$$T(37)=15+(60)e^{-1.887}$$

$$\approx24.0915$$

$$24.0915 < 30.$$

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Because $e^{-kt}\in(0,1)$ for finite $t>0$ and $T_0>T_a$,

$$T(t)-T_a=(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}>0.$$

Numerically $T(37)\approx24.0915>15$.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

The long-run limit of Newton's law is the ambient temperature, not $T_0$:

$$\lim_{t\to\infty}T(t)=T_a=15..$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Solve $T(t)=30$:

$$t=-\frac{1}{k}\ln\frac{30-15}{75-15}\approx27.1822$$

$$27.1822 < 37.$$

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Rearrange the model:

$$T(t)-T_a=(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}.$$

At $t=37$ the right-hand side equals $9.0915$, matching $T(37)-T_a$.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:
Newton cooling: $T(t)=T_a+(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}$ with $T_0=75$, $T_a=15$, $k=0.051$.

$$T(37)=15+(75-15)e^{-0.051\cdot37}\approx24.0915.$$

Time to reach $30$ solves $t=-\ln\frac{30-T_a}{T_0-T_a}/k\approx27.1822$.

tasks.title: Doubling time — exact versus rule of 72

$$\left|\frac{0.72}{r}-t\right|=\left|24-23.4498\right|\approx0.5502$$

So the statement is True.

tasks.title: Solace — GDP per capita force trap
tasks.context: In Solace, aggregate real GDP (billions of dollars) follows $Y(t)=500\,e^{0.026t}$ while population (millions) follows $N(t)=10\,e^{0.006t}$. Analysts track GDP per capita $y=Y/N$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Real GDP per capita grows at continuous annual force exactly $0.02$.
After $19$ years, GDP per capita exceeds $1.4$ times its initial level.
Because both GDP and population grow, the per-capita force equals $0.026+0.006$.

**A.** → True

$$\ln y(t)=\ln Y(t)-\ln N(t)$$

$$=\ln Y_0+gt-(\ln N_0+pt)$$

$$=\ln(Y_0/N_0)+(g-p)t$$

Hence the continuous force on $y$ is exactly $g-p=0.026-0.006=0.02$.

So the statement is True.

$$73.1142 > 70.$$

So the statement is False.

Compute the ratio of the recovered aggregate paths and compare with $y(19)$.

$$\frac{Y(19)}{N(19)}=\frac{819.4293}{11.2075}\approx73.1142$$

$$y(19)\approx73.1142$$

The absolute gap is about $0$, which is numerical noise, so the identity holds.

So the statement is True.

The additive-trap path would be

$$y_{\mathrm{wrong}}(t)=50\,e^{(0.026+0.006)t}\approx91.8377$$

while the true level is

$$y(19)\approx73.1142$$

$$91.8377 > 73.1142.$$

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:

$$y(t)=\frac{Y(t)}{N(t)}=50\,e^{(0.026-0.006)t}=50\,e^{0.02t}$$

$$y(19)\approx73.1142,\quad Y(19)\approx819.4293,\quad N(19)\approx11.2075.$$

tasks.title: Warden — piecewise force then solve for $t$
tasks.context: The Warden fund starts at $2000$ and grows continuously at force $0.038$ until $t=5$, then at force $0.018$. A covenant asks when the balance first reaches $2800$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The target level $2800$ is first reached at some time strictly after the rate switch $t=5$.
Ignoring the rate switch and extrapolating force $0.038$ all the way changes the hitting time.

Conditional on crossing after the switch, the remaining time equals $\ln(2800/f(5))/0.018$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

At the switch, $f(5)\approx2418.4992$. Compare with the target $2800$:

$$2418.4992 < 2800$$

Because the switch level is still below the target and $k_2=0.018>0$, solve

$$f(5)\,e^{0.018(t-5)}=2800$$

$$t=5+\frac{\ln(2800/2418.4992)}{0.018}\approx13.1373$$

Since $13.1373>5$, the first hitting time is after the switch.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Constant-force extrapolation with $k=0.038$ would solve

$$2000\,e^{0.038t}=2800$$

$$t=\frac{\ln(2800/2000)}{0.038}\approx8.8545$$

The piecewise hitting time is $\approx13.1373$. Those times differ, so ignoring the switch changes the answer.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Evaluate the piecewise path at the switch only.

$$f(5)\approx2418.4992$$

$$2418.4992 < 2800.$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

On $[0,5]$ the force is constant $k_1$, so

$$\frac{1}{T}\ln\frac{f(5)}{P_0}=\frac{1}{5}\ln\frac{2418.4992}{2000}$$

$$\approx0.038$$

which matches $k_1=0.038$.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

From $f(5)\,e^{k_2(t-T)}=2800$ take logs:

$$k_2(t-T)=\ln\frac{2800}{f(5)}$$

$$t-T=\frac{\ln(2800/f(5))}{0.018}$$

That is exactly.

So the statement is True.

tactical_explanations:

tasks.title: Newton cooling — ambient trap
tasks.context: A cup cools under Newton's law $T(t)=T_a+(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}$ with $T_0=75$, ambient $T_a=15$, and $k=0.051$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=37$ the temperature is strictly below $30$.
At $t=37$ the temperature remains strictly above ambient $T_a=15$.
It is not the case that as $t\to\infty$ the model temperature approaches the initial temperature $T_0$.
The temperature reaches $30$ at some time strictly before $t=37$.
The deviation from ambient at $t=37$ equals $(T_0-T_a)e^{-0.051\cdot37}$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Substitute into Newton's law.

$$T(37)=15+(60)e^{-1.887}$$

$$\approx24.0915$$

$$24.0915 < 30.$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Because $e^{-kt}\in(0,1)$ for finite $t>0$ and $T_0>T_a$,

$$T(t)-T_a=(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}>0.$$

Numerically $T(37)\approx24.0915>15$.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

The long-run limit of Newton's law is the ambient temperature, not $T_0$:

$$\lim_{t\to\infty}T(t)=T_a=15..$$

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Solve $T(t)=30$:

$$t=-\frac{1}{k}\ln\frac{30-15}{75-15}\approx27.1822$$

$$27.1822 < 37.$$

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Rearrange the model:

$$T(t)-T_a=(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}.$$

At $t=37$ the right-hand side equals $9.0915$, matching $T(37)-T_a$.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:
Newton cooling: $T(t)=T_a+(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}$ with $T_0=75$, $T_a=15$, $k=0.051$.

$$T(37)=15+(75-15)e^{-0.051\cdot37}\approx24.0915.$$

Time to reach $30$ solves $t=-\ln\frac{30-T_a}{T_0-T_a}/k\approx27.1822$.

tasks.title: Compound interest — continuous versus periodic
tasks.context: An account starts with principal $9000$ at nominal annual rate $r=0.076$. Compare continuous compounding with $14$ compoundings per year over $5$ years. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: After $5$ years the continuously compounded balance exceeds the balance with $14$ compounding periods per year.
With $14$ compoundings per year the $5$-year balance exceeds once-per-year compounding at the same nominal rate.
The absolute gap between continuous and $14$-per-year balances after $5$ years is less than $1\%$ of the discrete balance.
The effective annual rate under $14$ compoundings per year is strictly larger than the nominal rate $r=0.076$.

tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Compare the two recovered terminal balances.

$$A_{\mathrm{cont}}\approx13160.5613$$

$$A_{\mathrm{disc}}\approx13147.043$$

$$13160.5613 > 13147.043.$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Once-per-year compounding yields

$$P(1+r)^{t}=9000(1+0.076)^{5}\approx12980.872$$

while $14$-per-year compounding yields $\approx13147.043$.

$$13147.043 > 12980.872.$$

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Relative gap:

$$\frac{|A_{\mathrm{cont}}-A_{\mathrm{disc}}|}{A_{\mathrm{disc}}}\approx0.001028$$

Compare with $0.01$:

$$0.001028 < 0.01.$$

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

The EAR identity is

$$\mathrm{EAR}=\left(1+\frac{r}{n}\right)^{n}-1\approx0.078741.$$

For $n>1$ and $r>0$, EAR $>r$. Here $r=0.076$, so

$$0.078741 > 0.076.$$

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Continuous doubling solves $e^{rt}=2$.

$$t=\frac{\ln 2}{r}\approx9.1204$$

$$9.1204 < 12.$$

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:
Principal $P=9000$ at nominal annual rate $r=0.076$.

$$A_{\mathrm{disc}}=P\left(1+\frac{r}{n}\right)^{nt}=\left(1+\frac{0.076}{14}\right)^{70}\cdot9000\approx13147.043$$

$$6.6752 < 15.$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

By definition of half-life under $m(t)=m_0 e^{-kt}$,

$$m(T_{1/2})=\tfrac12 m_0\implies e^{-k T_{1/2}}=\tfrac12$$

$$k=\frac{\ln 2}{T_{1/2}}=\frac{\ln 2}{13}\approx0.053319..$$

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

One eighth remains after exactly three half-lives. Here

$$\frac{t}{T_{1/2}}=2.8462$$

and $m_0/8=6$. The actual remainder is $6.6752$, so the claim fails.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

From the overview, $m(37)=6.6752$. Compare with $5$:

$$6.6752 > 5.$$

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Solve $m(t)=5$ under the recovered $k$.

$$48\,e^{-kt}=5$$

So the statement is False.

tasks.title: Polar — GDP per capita force trap
tasks.context: In Polar, aggregate real GDP (billions of dollars) follows $Y(t)=500\,e^{0.026t}$ while population (millions) follows $N(t)=10\,e^{0.006t}$. Analysts track GDP per capita $y=Y/N$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Real GDP per capita grows at continuous annual force different from $0.02$.
After $19$ years, GDP per capita does not exceed $1.4$ times its initial level.
Because both GDP and population grow, the per-capita force equals $0.026+0.006$.
The identity $y(t)=Y(t)/N(t)$ holds at $t=19$ for the recovered paths.
Using force $0.026+0.006$ for per capita overstates the true $y(19)$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Take natural logs of the ratio definition.

$$\ln y(t)=\ln Y(t)-\ln N(t)$$

$$=\ln Y_0+gt-(\ln N_0+pt)$$

$$=\ln(Y_0/N_0)+(g-p)t$$

Hence the continuous force on $y$ is exactly $g-p=0.026-0.006=0.02$.

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

The overview recovered $y(19)\approx73.1142$ and $y_0=50$.

$$1.4\,y_0=70$$

$$y(19)=50\,e^{0.02\cdot19}\approx73.1142$$

$$73.1142 > 70.$$

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Adding the two forces would describe a product $Y\cdot N$, not the ratio $Y/N$.

$$\frac{d}{dt}\ln(Y/N)=g-p=0.02$$

$$g+p=0.032.$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Compute the ratio of the recovered aggregate paths and compare with $y(19)$.

$$\frac{Y(19)}{N(19)}=\frac{819.4293}{11.2075}\approx73.1142$$

$$y(19)\approx73.1142$$

The absolute gap is about $0$, which is numerical noise, so the identity holds.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

The additive-trap path would be

$$y_{\mathrm{wrong}}(t)=50\,e^{(0.026+0.006)t}\approx91.8377$$

while the true level is

$$y(19)\approx73.1142$$

$$91.8377 > 73.1142.$$

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:
Aggregate real GDP (billions) follows $Y(t)=500\,e^{0.026t}$ while population (millions) follows $N(t)=10\,e^{0.006t}$. GDP per capita is the ratio

$$y(t)=\frac{Y(t)}{N(t)}=50\,e^{(0.026-0.006)t}=50\,e^{0.02t}$$

So the continuous per-capita force is the difference $g-p=0.02$, not a sum. At $t=19$:

$$y(19)\approx73.1142,\quad Y(19)\approx819.4293,\quad N(19)\approx11.2075.$$

tasks.title: Competing continuous and discrete forecasts
tasks.context: Two forecasts start at $200$: continuous $f(t)=200\,e^{0.02t}$ and discrete $g(t)=200\,(1.025)^{t}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=15$ the continuous model exceeds the discrete base-$1.025$ model.
The continuous force $0.02$ exceeds $\ln(1.025)$.
At $t=15$ the two models differ by less than $5\%$ relative to the larger value.
The continuous model doubles strictly sooner than the discrete model.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Read the two terminal levels from the overview (or the figure).

$$f(15)\approx269.9718$$

$$g(15)\approx289.6596$$

$$269.9718 \le 289.6596.$$

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Compute the discrete force and compare with $k$.

$$\ln(1.025)\approx0.024693$$

$$0.02 \le 0.024693.$$

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Relative gap against the larger level:

$$\frac{|f-g|}{\max(f,g)}\approx0.067969$$

$$0.067969 \ge 0.05.$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

$$t_{\mathrm{cont}}=\frac{\ln 2}{0.02}\approx34.6574$$

$$t_{\mathrm{disc}}=\frac{\ln 2}{\ln(1.025)}\approx28.071$$

$$34.6574 \ge 28.071.$$

So the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Algebraically,

$$\ln\frac{Pe^{kt}}{P a^{t}}=(k-\ln a)t$$

$$=(0.02-0.024693)\cdot15\approx-0.070389.$$

Direct evaluation of $\ln(f/g)$ recovers the same number, so the identity holds.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:
Continuous forecast $f(t)=200e^{0.02t}$ versus discrete $g(t)=200(1.025)^{t}$. At $t=15$:

$$f(15)\approx269.9718,\quad g(15)\approx289.6596.$$

Equivalent discrete force $\ln(1.025)\approx0.024693$. Doubling times $34.6574$ (continuous) and $28.071$ (discrete).

tasks.title: Newton cooling — ambient trap
tasks.context: A cup cools under Newton's law $T(t)=T_a+(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}$ with $T_0=75$, ambient $T_a=15$, and $k=0.051$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=37$ the temperature is not strictly below $30$.
At $t=37$ the temperature remains not strictly above ambient $T_a=15$.
As $t\to\infty$ the model temperature approaches the initial temperature $T_0$.
The temperature reaches $30$ at some time strictly before $t=37$.
The deviation from ambient at $t=37$ does not equal $(T_0-T_a)e^{-0.051\cdot37}$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Substitute into Newton's law.

$$T(37)=15+(60)e^{-1.887}$$

$$\approx24.0915$$

$$24.0915 < 30.$$

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Because $e^{-kt}\in(0,1)$ for finite $t>0$ and $T_0>T_a$,

$$T(t)-T_a=(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}>0.$$

Numerically $T(37)\approx24.0915>15$.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

The long-run limit of Newton's law is the ambient temperature, not $T_0$:

$$\lim_{t\to\infty}T(t)=T_a=15..$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Solve $T(t)=30$:

$$t=-\frac{1}{k}\ln\frac{30-15}{75-15}\approx27.1822$$

$$27.1822 < 37.$$

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Rearrange the model:

$$T(t)-T_a=(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}.$$

At $t=37$ the right-hand side equals $9.0915$, matching $T(37)-T_a$.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Newton cooling: $T(t)=T_a+(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}$ with $T_0=75$, $T_a=15$, $k=0.051$.

$$T(37)=15+(75-15)e^{-0.051\cdot37}\approx24.0915.$$

Time to reach $30$ solves $t=-\ln\frac{30-T_a}{T_0-T_a}/k\approx27.1822$.

tasks.title: Bacterial culture — period growth
tasks.context: A culture starts at $N_0=1000$ and multiplies by $2$ every $3$ hours: $N(t)=1000(2)^{t/3}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=11$ the culture exceeds $20000$ individuals.
It is not the case that the continuous force $k=\ln(2)/3$ reproduces $N(t)$ for all $t$.
It is not the case that the elapsed time $t=11$ covers strictly more than three full growth periods of length $3$.
The culture doubles in every single growth period of length $3$.
The culture reaches $20000$ individuals at some time strictly before $t=11$.
tactical_explanations:
**B.** → False

Rewrite the period model as an exponential:

$$(2)^{t/3}=e^{(t/3)\ln(2)}=e^{kt}$$

with $k=\ln(2)/3\approx0.231049$. Thus the continuous force reproduces $N(t)$ identically.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

$$\frac{t}{\text{period}}=\frac{11}{3}=3.6667$$

$$3.6667 > 3.$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Each period multiplies by $2$, not necessarily by $2$. Doubling every period would require factor $2$. Here the factor is $2$, so the claim holds.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Solve $N(t)=20000$:

$$t=\frac{\ln(20000/1000)}{k}\approx12.9658$$

$$12.9658 \ge 11.$$

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: $N(t)=1000\cdot(2)^{t/3}$. Equivalent continuous force $k=\ln(2)/3\approx0.231049$. At $t=11$, after $3.6667$ growth periods, $N\approx12699.2084$. Time to reach $20000$ is $t=\ln(20000/1000)/k\approx12.9658$.

tasks.title: Change of base inside an exponential solve
tasks.context: Relate powers of $125$ and $5$ by solving $125^{x}=5^{3}$ with a change-of-base logarithm. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: $\log_{5}(125)$ is not an integer.
It is not the case that the solution of $125^{x}=5^{3}$ is $x=3/\log_{5}(125)$.
That solution is not strictly smaller than $3$.
Substituting the solved $x$ recovers equality of the two exponential sides.
$\log_{5}(125)$ is not strictly larger than $2$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$\log_{5}(125)=\frac{\ln 125}{\ln 5}=3$$

An integer check: distance to nearest integer is $0$, so the claim fails.

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Take $\log_{5}$ of both sides of $125^{x}=5^{3}$:

$$x\log_{5} a=3$$

$$x=\frac{3}{\log_{5} a}.$$

With $\log_{5} a=3$ this is $x=1$.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

$$x=1$$

$$1 < 3.$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$a^{x}=125^{1}\approx125$$

$$b^{3}=5^{3}=125$$

The sides match within numerical tolerance.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$3 > 2.$$

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Change-of-base identity: $\log_{5}(125)=\ln a/\ln b=3$. The equation $125^{x}=5^{3}$ becomes

$$x\log_{5} a=3\implies x=\frac{3}{\log_{5}(125)}=1.$$

Substitution recovers $125^{x}=5^{3}$.

tasks.title: Quadratic in a logarithm
tasks.context: Solve $1(\log_{10} x)^{2}+(-5)\log_{10} x+(6)=0$ for real $x>0$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Both recovered solutions for $x$ are not strictly positive.
The sum of the logarithmic roots $u$ does not equal $5$.
The product of the two $x$-solutions does not equal $10^{u_1+u_2}$.
$x=0$ is an admissible solution of the original logarithmic equation.
The product of the logarithmic roots $u$ equals $6$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$x_1=10^{2}\approx100,\quad x_2=10^{3}\approx1000.$$

Both are powers of a positive base, hence strictly positive.

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

For $u^{2}+\cdots=0$, Vieta gives $u_1+u_2=-c_1/c_2$.

$$u_1+u_2=2+3=5$$

$$-c_1/c_2=5.$$

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

$$x_1 x_2=b^{u_1}b^{u_2}=b^{u_1+u_2}.$$

Numerically $x_1 x_2\approx100000$ and $b^{u_1+u_2}\approx100000$.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

The logarithm $\log_{10} x$ is defined only for $x>0$. Therefore $x=0$ is not in the domain and cannot be a solution.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Vieta: $u_1 u_2=c_0/c_2=6$.

$$(2)(3)=6.$$

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:
Set $u=\log_{10} x$. The equation becomes

$$1u^{2}+(-5)u+(6)=0$$

with roots $u=2$ and $u=3$. Hence $x=10^{2}=100$ and $x=10^{3}=1000$. Domain requires $x>0$.

tasks.title: Elasticity — log-linear demand
tasks.context: Demand obeys $\ln Q = 5 - 1.5\ln P$ for $P>0$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: It is not the case that the price elasticity of demand is the constant $-1.5$.
At price $P=4$, quantity does not exceed $8$.
At that same price, $\ln Q$ is not strictly larger than $1$.
Demand is price-elastic in the sense $|\varepsilon|>1$.
It is not the case that doubling the price multiplies quantity by exactly $2^{-1.5}$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Differentiate the log-linear specification:

$$\frac{d\ln Q}{d\ln P}=-1.5.$$

That derivative is the elasticity, constant along the curve.

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

$$Q=e^{5-1.5\ln(4)}\approx18.5516$$

$$18.5516 > 8.$$

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

$$\ln Q\approx2.9206$$

$$2.9206 > 1.$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$|\varepsilon|=b=1.5$$

$$1.5 > 1.$$

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$\frac{Q(2P)}{Q(P)}=\frac{e^{a-b\ln(2P)}}{e^{a-b\ln P}}=2^{-b}\approx0.353553.$$

The constant-elasticity structure forces exactly that factor.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Log-linear demand $\ln Q=5-1.5\ln P$. At $P=4$,

$$\ln Q=5-1.5\ln(4)\approx2.9206\implies Q\approx18.5516.$$

Price elasticity is the constant $d\ln Q/d\ln P=-1.5$. Doubling price multiplies $Q$ by $2^{-1.5}\approx0.353553$.

tasks.title: Recover continuous force from two levels
tasks.context: A continuously growing stock satisfies $P(0)=500$ and $P(6)=800$. Recover the force $k$ in $P(t)=P_0 e^{kt}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The recovered continuous force does not exceed $0.04$.
It is not the case that substituting the recovered $k$ reproduces $P(6)=800$.
The doubling time under the recovered force is not strictly less than $20$.
The continuous force equals the linearised rate $(800-500)/(500\cdot6)$.
The linearised rate exceeds the true continuous force $k$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$k=\frac{\ln(1.6)}{6}\approx0.078334$$

$$0.078334 > 0.04.$$

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

$$P_0 e^{kt}=500\,e^{0.078334\cdot6}\approx800$$

which matches the observed $800$.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

$$t_{\times 2}=\frac{\ln 2}{k}\approx8.8486$$

$$8.8486 < 20.$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

$$k_{\mathrm{lin}}=0.1,\quad k=0.078334.$$

They differ; continuous force uses a logarithm, not a relative level change over $t$.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$0.1 > 0.078334.$$

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:
Observed $P(0)=500$ and $P(6)=800$ under continuous growth $P(t)=P_0 e^{kt}$. Recover

$$k=\frac{\ln(P_t/P_0)}{t}=\frac{\ln(800/500)}{6}\approx0.078334.$$

Doubling time $\ln 2/k\approx8.8486$. A linearised rate $(P_t-P_0)/(P_0 t)\approx0.1$ is not $k$.

tasks.title: Reading a logarithmic graph
tasks.context: The figure shows $f(x)=\log_{2}(x)$. Use the graph together with logarithm identities to judge each claim. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: On the graph, $f(2)$ is strictly less than $1$.
The graph crosses the horizontal axis at $x=0$.
The graphed function is not strictly increasing on $(0,\infty)$.
At $x=2$ the graph reads exactly $1$.
The vertical reading at $x=4$ is not exactly twice the reading at $x=2$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$f(2)=\log_{2} 2=\frac{\ln 2}{\ln(2)}\approx1$$

$$1 \ge 1$$

(Equivalently, $f(2)<1$ iff the base exceeds $2$.).

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

By definition $\log_{2} 1=0$, so the graph meets $y=0$ at $x=1$. That intercept is visible on the figure and required by the logarithm identity.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

For base $2>1$ the logarithm is strictly increasing: if $0<x_1<x_2$ then $\log_{2} x_1<\log_{2} x_2$. The base exceeds 1, so the claim fails.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$\log_{2}(2)=1$$

exactly, which is the standard normalisation of the logarithm.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$f(4)=\log_{2}(2^{2})=2\log_{2} 2=2f(2).$$

Numerically $f(4)\approx2$ and $2f(2)\approx2$.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: The figure shows $f(x)=\log_{2}(x)$ for $x>0$. Key calibrations: $f(1)=0$, $f(2)=1$, and $f(2)\approx1$. Because $\log_{2}(x^{2})=2\log_{2} x$, $f(4)=2f(2)\approx2$.

tasks.title: Richter scale — amplitude versus energy proxy
tasks.context: Two earthquakes have Richter magnitudes $4.5$ and $6.5$. Amplitude scales as $10^{M}$; a standard energy proxy scales as $10^{1.5M}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The amplitude ratio between the larger and smaller quake exceeds $100$.
The energy-proxy ratio exceeds the amplitude ratio.
The amplitude ratio equals the raw magnitude gap $2$.
$\log_{10}$ of the amplitude ratio recovers exactly the magnitude gap.
The magnitude gap exceeds $2$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$\frac{A_2}{A_1}=10^{2}\approx100$$

$$100 \le 100.$$

So the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$\frac{E_2}{E_1}\approx1000,\quad \frac{A_2}{A_1}\approx100$$

$$1000 > 100.$$

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

The magnitude gap is $2$, but amplitudes scale exponentially:

$$\frac{A_2}{A_1}=10^{\Delta M}\approx100\neq2..$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$\log_{10}(A_2/A_1)=m_2-m_1=2.$$

That is the defining inversion of the Richter amplitude scale.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$2 \le 2.$$

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Richter amplitude scales as $A\propto 10^{M}$. Between magnitudes $4.5$ and $6.5$,

$$\frac{A_2}{A_1}=10^{6.5-4.5}=100.$$

A common energy proxy uses $E\propto 10^{1.5 M}$, so

tasks.title: Change of base inside an exponential solve

Substitution recovers $125^{x}=5^{3}$.

tasks.title: Log product/quotient in a calibrated ratio
tasks.context: Simplify $\log_{3}\dfrac{9\cdot27}{3}$ using logarithm algebra. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.

tasks.title: pH — logarithmic concentration gap

tasks.title: Quadratic in a logarithm
tasks.context: Solve $1(\log_{e} x)^{2}+(-3)\log_{e} x+(2)=0$ for real $x>0$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Both recovered solutions for $x$ are strictly positive.
The sum of the logarithmic roots $u$ equals $3$.
The product of the two $x$-solutions equals $e^{u_1+u_2}$.
$x=0$ is an admissible solution of the original logarithmic equation.
The product of the logarithmic roots $u$ equals $2$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$x_1=e^{1}\approx2.718282,\quad x_2=e^{2}\approx7.389056.$$

Both are powers of a positive base, hence strictly positive.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

For $u^{2}+\cdots=0$, Vieta gives $u_1+u_2=-c_1/c_2$.

$$u_1+u_2=1+2=3$$

$$-c_1/c_2=3.$$

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$x_1 x_2=b^{u_1}b^{u_2}=b^{u_1+u_2}.$$

Numerically $x_1 x_2\approx20.085537$ and $b^{u_1+u_2}\approx20.085537$.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → False

The logarithm $\log_{e} x$ is defined only for $x>0$. Therefore $x=0$ is not in the domain and cannot be a solution.

So the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Vieta: $u_1 u_2=c_0/c_2=2$.

$$(1)(2)=2.$$

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:
Set $u=\log_{e} x$. The equation becomes

$$1u^{2}+(-3)u+(2)=0$$

with roots $u=1$ and $u=2$. Hence $x=e^{1}=2.718282$ and $x=e^{2}=7.389056$. Domain requires $x>0$.

tasks.title: Recover continuous force from two levels

$$k=\frac{\ln(1.6)}{6}\approx0.078334$$

$$t_{\times 2}=\frac{\ln 2}{k}\approx8.8486$$

$$8.8486 < 20.$$

So the statement is False.

**D.** → False

tasks.context: Demand obeys $\ln Q = 3.5 - 0.8\ln P$ for $P>0$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.

tasks.title: Reading a logarithmic graph

tasks.context: A balance starts at $1000$. Compare continuous force $k=0.018$ with discrete annual base $1.02$ when chasing target $1500$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The continuous model reaches $1500$ not strictly sooner than the discrete model.
The one-year continuous multiplier $e^{0.018}$ differs from the discrete base $1.02$.
The continuous hitting time is strictly less than $25$.
It is not the case that both models share the same hitting time for target $1500$.
Substituting the continuous hitting time recovers the target balance.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$22.5258 \ge 20.4753.$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$e^{0.018}\approx1.018163,\quad a=1.02.$$

They differ, so continuous and discrete paths are not reparametrisations of each other.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$22.5258 < 25.$$

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Hitting times $22.5258$ versus $20.4753$ are unequal.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

$$P e^{k t}= 1000 e^{0.018\cdot22.5258}\approx1500..$$

So the statement is True.

tasks.title: Exam mashup — elasticity beside exponential stock
tasks.context: Demand follows $\ln Q=5-1.4\ln P$. Separately a stock follows $N(t)=200e^{0.044t}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Demand is price-elastic ($|\varepsilon|>1$).
At the stated price, quantity exceeds $5$.
At $t=11$ the growing stock exceeds $1.4$ times its initial level.
The demand elasticity does not equal the stock's continuous force $0.044$.
The stock's force recovered from $N(11)/N_0$ equals $0.044$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$|\varepsilon|=1.4 > 1.$$

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

$$Q\approx31.8789$$

$$31.8789 > 5.$$

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

$$N(11)\approx324.5103,\quad 1.4 N_0=280.$$

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Elasticity $1.4$ and force $0.044$ are unrelated parameters from different models.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

$$\frac{1}{t}\ln\frac{N(11)}{N_0}=0.044..$$

So the statement is True.
